reason: This looks like an optional compensation / filtering capacitor between the output node and an internal RC node (net44). If removed, the core differential/active-load functionality remains; you mainly lose extra stability/noise filtering provided by that pole/zero shaping.
impact_estimate: Low–Medium: DC gain/bias largely unchanged; transient response and phase margin may worsen depending on load and the R-network around net44.

reason: R2 likely serves only to reference net44 to ground as part of an output RC network (together with C0 and possibly R0/R1/R3). If C0 is removed, net44 no longer influences the signal path meaningfully, so R2 can usually be removed as well.
impact_estimate: Low (if C0 removed first): Minimal effect on amplifier operation; caveat—if any other element uses net44 for biasing, keep R2.

reason: R3 appears to be an explicit output load (a shunt from VOUT1 to ground) used for testbench/loading rather than for setting the amplifier’s internal bias. Removing it generally preserves amplifier functionality, but changes the loading and therefore output swing, gain, and operating point under load.
impact_estimate: Low–Medium: Core operation remains; output DC level and small-signal gain can shift due to lighter loading (depends on whether another load is present externally).
